newsitem.title: USA: Canada LPG market sags, following U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Canada LPG market sags, following U.S. markets.

text.p: Canada liquified petroleum gases (LPG) sagged this week on the lead of U.S. markets but players said Thursday they were unsure which direction Canada will take given cold weather ahead.
"No one seems to know which direction we could go, with the colder weather we could come up five cents, but with Belvieu (in Texas) down, we could go down five cents," said one East Canadian trader.
The Canadian markets are closely tied to the U.S., particulary the western hub of Edmonton which is hooked to the Midcontinent via pipelines.

Players reported that due to warm weather in December propane previously under January contractual obligations in the east were instead continuing to be shipped through pipelines from Edmonton into Conway, Kansas.
"The forecast for pipeline deliveries (into the east) are being reduced," said a Canadian LPG trader.
In Eastern Canada, spot Sarnia propane edged down a half cent to between 64.00 cents and 65.50 cents a gallon. Edmonton spot product in the west showed more uncertainty with a lower, but wide range.
Edmonton was trading between 66.00/68.00 cents, three cents below last Thursday.
Meanwhile, the butane market remained quiet in both hubs except for the constant year-round demand by refineries in the northern tier states who blend Edmonton field butane with gasoline.
Edmonton field butane was about one cent lower to 48.50/50.00 cents. --(Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631))
